regime.headline: Hawkish repricing
regime.paragraph: Rates markets priced a more hawkish policy path: US Treasury yields 2Y +14bp to 4.88% and 10Y +13bp to 5.13%. The US curve saw a parallel sell-off with 2s10s unch. The dollar rose 0.3%, gold fell 2.8%, the S&P 500 fell 0.3% and Brent rose 3.8%. US high-yield spreads tightened 4bp. The standout move was Euro HY credit spread (OAS) (-19bp, 2.5x its 20-day volatility).

relationships.lesson: Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it. A break often reflects central-bank buying, geopolitical hedging or dollar moves.

relationships.statement: Wider Treasury–Bund spreads favoured USD over EUR.
relationships.lesson: FX tends to follow relative rates: a wider US–German yield gap raises the carry on USD versus EUR. Front-end (2Y) differentials usually matter more than 10Y.

relationships.statement: Higher US yields supported the dollar.
relationships.lesson: Higher US yields raise the return on dollar assets and attract capital. When the dollar moves against yields, risk sentiment or non-US news is usually driving FX instead.
Energy feeds directly into headline inflation, so short-dated breakevens track oil closely.

relationships.statement: Gilts underperformed Bunds, pointing to UK-specific drivers such as data, BoE pricing or fiscal supply.
relationships.lesson: Cross-market spreads strip out the global rates move, isolating what was local.

relationships.statement: Copper and Chinese equities fell together, pointing to softer China growth sentiment.
relationships.lesson: China consumes about half the world's copper, so the metal is a real-time proxy for Chinese industrial demand.

interview.question: Why did Bunds outperform Treasuries?
interview.answer: 10Y Treasuries moved +13bp versus unch for Bunds, so the spread moved +13bp to 181bp (99th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: Was today's Treasury sell-off driven by real yields or inflation expectations?
interview.answer: Nominal yields rose 13.4bp, driven by real yields (real +12.0bp, breakeven +4.0bp). Nominal yield = real yield + breakeven inflation. Real-yield-led moves usually reflect policy expectations or growth; breakeven-led moves reflect inflation risk, often energy prices. Brent moved +3.8%.

interview.question: Why did Bunds outperform Gilts?
interview.answer: 10Y Gilts moved +9bp versus unch for Bunds, so the spread moved +8bp to 198bp (95th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.

interview.question: Why did the dollar strengthen?
interview.answer: DXY moved +0.3% alongside a +13bp move in 10Y Treasuries and +13bp in the US–Germany 2Y spread. The textbook link is relative rates: higher US yields versus the rest of the world raise the carry on USD.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Federal Reserve, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 100% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 4.0 hikes (99bp) over 12 months; terminal 5.13%. The 12-month pricing moved +9bp on the day. Method: Refinitiv OIS curve. Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +99bp is 4.0 moves.
